jess: Quick heads-up — FP8 profile (profile-id: fp8-v2-compact) rolled to staging yesterday and our semantic correctness metric for the search-assistant prompt family jumped down ~1.8% over 6h. Not catastrophic but above our guardrail.
raj: Which metric exactly? and what's the baseline window?
jess: metric = `semantically_correct_rate` (eval harness); baseline = last 7 days at the same traffic mix. Canary build: 2026-03-18T22:12 (model: redwood-7b.fp8).
nate: Do we have per-prompt-family deltas? Might be a narrow reg hitting only long-instruction examples.
jess: Yes — the drop is concentrated on instruction-heavy queries (long context > 1k tokens). Short prompts look fine.
sophia: If it's long-context only we should *not* do a full rollback yet. We should add a runtime safety gate: require a `precision_profile` hint and shadow-eval traffic for fp8. Also clarify an API surface for customers to opt-out per-endpoint.
alex: For telemetry we need a histogram of response-delta vs fp32 baseline and token-level divergence counts. I can add a Grafana panel. Query example (pseudo):
```
sum(rate(response_delta_count{profile="fp8-v2-compact",prompt_family="search-assistant"}[5m])) by (bucket)
```
This gives us a quick shape.
raj: What's our intended rollback policy? autos? manual?
jess: Ops suggestion: if `semantically_correct_rate` drops >1% AND sustained for 30m on production canary -> auto-rollback to previous quant profile, with notification. For staging we keep in shadow for 48h until we have diff reports.
qc-bot: Shadow reports scheduled: run nightly partial replays (10k samples) and post `delta-summary` to #qc.
nate: Implementation plan idea: 1) enable fp8-v2 in `shadow-mode` in runtime; 2) collect per-request `delta_hash` + quality score; 3) produce per-model/per-prompt-family report; 4) gate rollout by per-prompt-family pass rates.
sophia: Small API suggestion: add header `X-Precision-Mode: default|strict|shadow` that the client or internal router can set. `default` = current stable behaviour, `strict` forces fp32-equivalent safety checks, `shadow` executes quant variant but does not serve it. This is lighter than adding heavy per-request flags in the RPC.
alex: I'd rather metadata live in model manifest (model_config.precision_advisory) than as a runtime header for most cases — headers for overrides only. Runtime boundary: manifest sets default advisory, request header can be used for overrides.
raj: Sounds reasonable. How intrusive is this for runtime? need compatibility with Dedicated/private too.
sophia: Minimal change: runtime already supports per-request metadata. We need to serialize evasion tags through the routing layer and have the agent read `precision_advisory`. For Dedicated, the control-plane will push model manifest entries.
jess: Also we need a lightweight scorer that can run in parallel (cheap) to compute `semantic_delta` without full eval (embedding cosine + classifier). That lets us triage faster.
nate: Ops note: latency impact of parallel shadow scoring should be asynchronous; don't block response path. Memory overhead for fp8 (KV shapes) looks fine — measured ~3% more transient memory in staging.
oncall-bot: Canary monitor active: fp8-v2-compact -> staging canary group (10%). Alerts: configured on `%delta <= -1.0` for semantically_correct_rate.
jess: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC for the API header + runtime manifest field, plus an ops playbook for shadow-mode evaluation. I can own the RFC and pairing with @sophia and @alex as reviewers.
sophia: :thumbsup: please include acceptance criteria: telemetry panels, nightly shadow report, auto-rollback rule.
alex: I'll add the Grafana panels and a PromQL dashboard for delta histograms.
nate: I'll prep the ops checklist and the script for nightly partial replays.
raj: Let's aim to merge the runtime changes behind a feature flag so we can toggle per-cluster. Also add a compatibility lint to prevent older SDKs from inadvertently setting restrictive headers.
jess: Great — I'll open the RFC PR today and tag reviewers. Thanks all.
qc-bot: Night replay scheduled at 02:00 UTC — will post deltas in #qc tomorrow.
